events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWLUB

The National Weather Service in Lubbock has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Crosby County in northwestern Texas...
Central Lubbock County in northwestern Texas...

* Until 800 AM CDT.

* At 607 AM CDT, the public reported flash flooding across the warned
area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour. Additional rainfall
amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lubbock, Wolfforth, Idalou, Lubbock International Airport, Downtown
Lubbock, Texas Tech University, Lubbock South Plains Mall, Cone and
Lubbock Science Spectrum.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Yellow House Draw, North Fork Double Mountain Fork Brazos River,
Blackwater Draw and Crawfish Creek.

events.region: Dalton Highway Summits; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow and gusty winds expected. Total snow accumulations of 2
to 5 inches with locally higher amounts above pass level. Winds
gusting up to around 30 to 40 mph.

* WHERE...Dalton, Elliott, and Steese Highway Summits, White
Mountains, and Higher Terrain South of the Yukon River.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of fronts will lift north over the
Interior Thursday into Friday, with the strongest winds expected
Thursday into Thursday night. Winds will lessen on Friday as snow
chances persist.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...TROPICAL DEPRESSION CHAMPI MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Guam is now in Condition of Readiness 3, meaning damaging winds are
possible within 48 hours.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon watch continues for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 7 PM ChST...the center of Tropical Depression Champi (29W) was
located near latitude 11.0N...longitude 157.8E. This was about
890 miles east of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest,
285 degrees, at 10 mph. Storm intensity was 35 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
It is vital that you do not focus on the exact forecast track. To
do so could result in bad decisions and place you or those you
are responsible for at greater risk. Tropical Depression 29W is
currently moving west-northwest, but is expected to make a turn
toward the west Friday.

Damaging winds are likely within Guam and the Northern Marianas late
Saturday night and Sunday. At this time it appears that the strongest
winds will be towards the southernmost islands. Islands near the
center should prepare for typhoon force winds, with the latest JTWC
forecast showing sustained winds of roughly 85 knots.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

and Kosrae that the heavy rainfall and gusty winds have weakened.

further away. Therefore, this will be the last special weather
statement issuance. However, a Small Craft Advisory remains in

above that, along with elevated, choppy seas.
